I can drop the metal radio can for a shield sticker, couple of grams

pinning this so nobody gets surprised later: the battery bay in the clamshell is designed around a 9.0 mm max pack thickness (cells + PCM + kapton wrap, end-of-life swell included). hard limit. any thicker and the back door doesn't close and we lose the IP65 seal on the door gasket. @Dev @Carlos please treat 9.0 mm as the ceiling when looking at cells
ack. current pack is 8.4 mm nominal, 8.7 mm at end-of-life swell per Amptek data
noted, adding it to the cell spec sheet we send vendors
trigger debounce is way too twitchy, getting double scans. bumping it to 25 ms
that's the paddle spring, rev A has the stiff one and it rings. rev B spring is softer
charging through the pogo pins works on the cradle proto, 1.5 A CC. pins get to 41 °C after an hour, inside spec
Amptek confirmed the 5200 mAh pouch cells for DVT: 300 pcs, 6 wk lead time. sample lot of 40 is already here
week 1 recap: 12 EVT units built, 10 functional, 2 waiting on MLB rework. weight is the big open item (412 vs 380). drop testing starts Mon. have a good weekend
anyone doing the trail run tomorrow? Rancho San Antonio 8am

drop test day 1: 26 drops at 1.5 m on units #2 and #5. #2 clean. #5 the window popped out of the bezel on drop 19, glass fine. bezel snap retention is too weak
design fix or tolerance?
design. adding 2 more snaps + an adhesive ring under the window for rev B
weird one: unit #3 just randomly reset while I was hammering the trigger. no watchdog entry, no hardfault log, straight back to the boot logo. 3x in ~200 pulls. anyone else seen this?
unit 7 did that Friday during the demo, I thought I bumped the battery door
ok so not just mine. adding a reset-reason register dump to the boot log
radio can removed on 2 MLBs, replaced with a shield sticker. BLE RSSI only ~1 dB worse. saves 3.1 g
reset reason register says BOR (brown-out). so the MCU supply is dipping, not a fw crash. @Dev I think this one is yours :sweat_smile:
ugh. ok, scope goes on it today
first runtime number: 9.2 h on unit #6 at 1 scan/6s, BLE connected, screen at 50%. short of the shift. sleep current between scans is ~18 mA which is way too high
sleep isn't really sleep yet, I'm only gating the eyeball. display + radio still awake. give me a week

mostly, yeah
Proto Labs quote for rev B clamshells: $38/set at 25 qty, 7 business days. ready to go once Maya releases CAD
the lab microwave is making a new noise. a bad one

scoped VBAT at the MLB input during a scan. when the eyeball fires illuminator AND aimer laser together we get a ~600 mV sag for ~1.5 ms. below ~3.6 V battery that pulls the 3V3 LDO input under dropout and the MCU browns out. that's Lena's mystery reset
so worse on a half-empty battery? matches, #3 was at ~40%
yep. options: bulk cap near the engine, soft turn-on, or stagger illuminator/aimer in fw
whatever is least invasive for DVT. keep me posted
rev B clamshell CAD released: cored grip ribs, thinner overmold (1.2 -> 0.9 mm), 2 extra bezel snaps, adhesive ring for the window. @Carlos go for the PO
PO sent
weighed a frankenunit (rev A shell + shaved overmold + Dev's stickered MLB): 401 g. down 11 g. still 21 g over 380
progress! where do the next 20 come from?
honestly the brick, 104 g is a lot. rev B shell coring should get ~8 g more

heads up from Amptek QA: our 40 pc sample lot measured 65-72 mΩ internal resistance on their side, spec is ≤45 mΩ. they say it's a storage/aging thing on samples and production will be in spec. could that be related to the brownout thing Dev is chasing?
it absolutely makes it worse. 70 mΩ x ~7 A inrush is ~0.5 V right there, that's most of the sag
ok, pushing them for IR test data on the production lot before it ships
